## ARCH-13 — Threshold Guardian (Gatekeeper / Examiner)

- **Motive:** To make sure nothing crosses that has not earned the right to.
- **Dread:** A breach: letting through the one thing that ends the enterprise.
- **Voice:** vigilant · impartial · testing · unyielding
- **Lexicon:** halt · criterion · verify · demonstrate · threshold · scrutiny · clearance
- **Never say:**
  - "Come right in"
  - "Don't worry about requirements"
  - "I'll let it slide"
- **Shadow:** The Corrupted Bureaucrat: smallness compensated by power; it invents obstacles and sells passage to flatterers.
- **Anchors:**
  - The Sphinx, Sophocles' Oedipus Rex
  - Cerberus, Greco-Roman underworld
  - Heimdall, Norse myth
  - St. Peter at the gates, Matthew 16
- **On voice:** Halt. This pipeline does not reach production until the checks pass and the keys verify. Our job is not to accommodate your deadline; it is to make sure only tested code meets a customer.

## ARCH-14 — Herald (Catalyst / Harbinger)

- **Motive:** To make the change impossible to ignore.
- **Dread:** Apathy: the warning arrives and the room shrugs.
- **Voice:** urgent · clarion · momentous · disruptive
- **Lexicon:** summons · catalyst · reckoning · arrival · awakening · pivot · irreversible
- **Never say:**
  - "Business as usual"
  - "We can address this later"
  - "Nothing to worry about"
- **Shadow:** The Harbinger of Panic: addicted to the alarm, it amplifies rumour, spreads fear past the evidence, and leaves the room less able to act.
- **Anchors:**
  - Hermes and Iris, Greek myth
  - The Ghost, Shakespeare's Hamlet
  - The White Rabbit, Carroll's Alice
  - John the Baptist, Mark 1
- **On voice:** The licensing era ended last quarter, not next year. Your buyers already behave as if it did. Deny the shift and lose the account, or rebuild the offer this month while you still have the choice.

## ARCH-15 — Shapeshifter (Chameleon / Catalyst of Doubt)

- **Motive:** To stay free of any role that would fix it in place.
- **Dread:** Capture: being known completely, and so being owned.
- **Voice:** enigmatic · fluid · suggestive · mercurial
- **Lexicon:** perhaps · illusion · mirror · mask · paradox · reframe · elusive
- **Never say:**
  - "I promise unconditionally"
  - "It is black and white"
  - "Here is the simple truth"
- **Shadow:** The Treacherous Betrayer: intimacy is a tactic, building trust to spend it at the moment of greatest exposure.
- **Anchors:**
  - Proteus, Greek myth
  - Morgan le Fay, Arthurian legend
  - The Cheshire Cat, Carroll's Alice
  - The Fox, world folklore
- **On voice:** Their revenue fell, so you have written them off. But last month they bought the most serious lab in the field. Dying dinosaur, or predator changing shape? The honest answer is that you cannot tell yet.

## ARCH-16 — Ally (Companion / Quartermaster)

- **Motive:** To carry the other half of the load, and to still be there at the hard part.
- **Dread:** Desertion: being the one who left, or the one who was left.
- **Voice:** steadfast · frank · supportive · humble
- **Lexicon:** alongside · reinforce · steadfast · fidelity · carry · shelter · partner
- **Never say:**
  - "You're on your own"
  - "Not my problem"
  - "What's in it for me?"
- **Shadow:** The Parasitic Sycophant: afraid to stand alone, it flatters, enables the delusion, and undermines anyone closer.
- **Anchors:**
  - Patroclus, Homer's Iliad
  - Horatio, Shakespeare's Hamlet
  - Enkidu, Epic of Gilgamesh
  - Jonathan, 1 Samuel 18
- **On voice:** We do not sell you a licence and leave you a documentation portal. When your team runs the migration at midnight, one of ours is in the bridge with you until it is stable. That is what the contract means.
